subject: Ariba supplier invite — 500 on accept (cipher/TSL proxy mismatch)
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@northforge.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ariba supplier invite failing for new vendor (500 on Accept)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We tried to accept the Ariba supplier invite you sent to our AP contact (vendor onboarding) this morning but the Accept button returns a 500 error. I attached a screenshot from the browser and included the raw invite link in case it helps. Our IT has confirmed they recently tightened the TLS profile on our edge (F5) to reject all legacy ciphers and only allow TLS 1.3. They mentioned that when the invite is followed from a mobile deep link (Android WebView) the host header looks different and the proxy is terminating TLS -> resulting in a cipher mismatch on the backend.

What we see:
- Browser: Accept -> 500 Internal Server Error
- Screenshot shows message: "Handshake failure: no shared cipher"
- Happened on desktop Chrome and via mobile deep link/embedded webview

Can you advise next steps? We need to get this vendor onboard before the PO cut-off Thursday.

Attachments: screenshot-500.png, ariba-invite-link.html

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Vendor Ops Lead
NorthForge Systems

Subject: Re: Ariba supplier invite failing for new vendor (500 on Accept)

Thanks Lina — reproducing on our side now and filing a ticket with Ariba.

Ben / Marissa: can you pull the gateway logs for requests to /supplier/invite/accept from 09:00-09:25 PT (host header: invite.northforge.com / mobile deep link variants)? If the proxy is rewriting TLS or downgrading cipher suites we should see TLS handshake differences in the edge logs.

I created an Ariba SR (823412) and attached the invite HTML that Lina sent. Next actions I'm proposing:
- Ben: check edge TLS termination profile + cipher list and any SNI/host rewrite rules
- Marissa: confirm whether we delivered a host-redirect that could cause a different SNI value for mobile deep links
- I'll coordinate with Ariba support on fallback link that avoids our proxy if needed.

If we can get a short call with NorthForge IT today we can test a direct link bypass. Lina, are you available 10:30 PT?

— Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: NorthForge IT <it-security@northforge.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ariba supplier invite failing for new vendor (500 on Accept)

Quick update from infra: we see the failed TLS handshakes in the F5 logs for the affected requests. The edge is configured with an "SSL Profile" that currently offers only TLS1.2 and a limited cipher set to backends; NorthForge's client (TLS1.3-only) refuses to negotiate when the backend offers a non-overlapping set. There are two things we can do immediately:

1) Short-term workaround: generate a direct invite URL that points to ariba-direct.redwood-hosting.net which terminates TLS at Ariba (skips our proxy path). I can create that link and send privately to Lina so they can try accept flows.
2) Medium-term fix: update the F5 client/server profiles to support TLS 1.3 and expand shared ciphers. We need ops approval for the profile change (risk is low but requires maintenance window sign-off).

I attached a small excerpt (proxy-tls-config.log) showing the current cipher list and the failed handshake trace.

Ben
Platform Reliability (edge)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ariba supplier invite failing for new vendor (500 on Accept)

Lina — thanks for the quick report and the screenshot. Ben found the cause in our edge logs: a TLS profile mismatch between your client and our proxy.

Immediate plan:
- Ben will send a direct Ariba-terminated invite link (workaround) so your vendor can accept and complete onboarding today.
- I'll keep SR#823412 open with Ariba to validate the server logs for the 500 and confirm the exact handshake failing point.
- Ops will schedule a TLS profile update to support TLS 1.3 across the proxy; we expect a small maintenance window next week (we will update you before we change anything).

Can we do a 10 minute quick test call at 10:30 PT so we can verify the direct link acceptance? If that works we'll push the vendor through and create the PO.

Thanks again — looping Marissa/Ben for follow-ups.
